title: openai /v1/chat.completions parity: params, roles, stop/logprobs, streaming & structured output
author: Asha Patel
description:
Bridge OpenAI /v1/chat.completions parity gaps: map OpenAI-style parameters (messages, roles, stop, max_tokens, logprobs) to Redwood internal API, stabilize streaming/chunking semantics, wire function/tool-calling fields through the compatibility layer, and ensure structured output + response_formatting matches OpenAI behavior. Motivation: several customers use the OpenAI-compatible endpoint and expect identical semantics for model selection, streaming delimiting, role handling, and logprobs/stop behavior. This PR consolidates compat-layer mapping, comprehensive E2E tests, and docs updates.

What changed (high level):
- Request mapping: canonicalize `messages` -> internal prompt pieces preserving roles and metadata, accept both `role` strings and legacy objects. Preserve `user`/`system`/`assistant` semantics.
- Parameter parity: add support for `stop` arrays/strings, `max_tokens` translation, `temperature`/`top_p` passthrough and fallbacks, and `logprobs` propagation to generation backend when requested.
- Streaming stability: fix chunk framing and newline-safe boundaries, ensure `delta` patching matches OpenAI streaming events when `stream=true`. Add backpressure handling and graceful connection close to avoid truncated JSON in structured output.
- Function/tool calling: forward `functions` schema and `function_call` hints into the internal tool-calling pipeline, and synthesize `tool_call` events for streaming responses when function invocation is produced by the model.
- Structured output & response formatting: ensure `response_formatting` and `formatting_engine` path produce identical `content`/`metadata` fields and that formatting failures surface as `finish_reason` values consistent with OpenAI.
- Tests & docs: new E2E fixtures under tests/openai/* and a compatibility doc with examples.

Why this approach: Rather than ad-hoc field translation in multiple places, we unify mapping in go/openai_compat/handler.go and add a single translation layer used by both hosted runtime and dedicated/private adapters. This reduces duplication and avoids drift as new OpenAI-like params are added.

Risks and mitigations:
- Streaming race: changing chunk boundaries risked truncated JSON. Mitigation: added a framing layer with explicit length-prefixed boundary for structured chunks and additional unit tests that replays real-world chunk sizes.
- Performance impact: extra mapping layer is lightweight; benchmarks show <1% median latency increase on small requests. Kept hot paths inlined for large streaming workloads.

Backwards compatibility: No API-breaking changes. Default behavior remains unchanged if OpenAI-compat params are not used.

Release notes:
- Added: OpenAI /v1/chat.completions parity for roles, stop/logprobs, streaming formatting, and function-calling glue. Improved OpenAI-compatible docs and added E2E tests.

release_notes: Added parity improvements for OpenAI /v1/chat.completions: roles/messages mapping, stop parameter support (string/array), logprobs propagation, streaming chunking/framing stability, and function/tool calling passthrough. Includes docs and E2E tests.
notes: This PR focuses on surface parity; further follow-ups will add more exhaustive logprob validation across model families and an audit of legacy user-role edge cases.
examples:
Request example: POST /v1/chat/completions { "messages": [{"role":"system","content":"You are a helpful assistant."},{"role":"user","content":"Write a haiku about latency."}], "model":"gpt-compat-1", "stream": true, "max_tokens": 60, "stop": ["
"], "logprobs": 5 }
Streaming note: chunks now emit either 'delta' events for text deltas, or length-prefixed JSON for structured events to avoid split-json issues across TCP boundaries.
Function call flow: when model emits function call, compat layer synthesizes a `tool_call` streaming event and preserves `name` + `arguments` as JSON string in the structured payload.
